title_en: Neuromancer Apple TV Series Comes to Streaming Early 2027 and It Looks Just as Intense as Its Source Material
summary_en: Apple TV's Neuromancer finally has a release date, along with a fast-paced first look at the highly-anticipated cyberpunk series.
body_en:
Apple TV's Neuromancer finally has a release date, along with a fast-paced first look at the highly anticipated cyberpunk series.
As revealed during the Apple TV panel in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, Neuromancer will come to the streaming service on Friday, January 22, 2027.
Showrunner and executive producer Graham Roland gave fans a few more details on what they can expect from the first-ever screen adaptation of William Gibson's genre-defining novel, explaining why now is the perfect time to bring it to life.
"42 years ago, this book felt like true science fiction," Roland said. "Gibson famously coined the term 'cyberspace' to describe a digital space where people in the book go to to escape and interact [with each other], and he did all that before the internet existed.
"He wrote about the collision of artificial intelligence and human intelligence before artificial intelligence existed. Now, we’re living in a world 40 years later where these things are a part of our everyday lives. It's an appropriate time to revisit the text, to put it in a new light now that these things are here."
Roland also shed some light on what it's been like working with Callum Turner, who plays the book's central character and resident console cowboy, Case. Notably, Roland said that Turner has a big love for Neuromancer, and confirmed that this series is focused on Case.
"Everyone came with a deep love of the source material," he said. "He read the book, dove into his character. Case is an atypical protagonist. He's a criminal, rough around the edges, he’s a survivor. In the book, there's no mention of his family, he’s kind of an orphan, doing out of an instinct of survival, desperation. Callum threads that needle. He's able to play the dangerous part of Case, inhabit the humanity and charisma. One of the things that's very important is that this is Case’s story, you’re following him. The charisma needs to carry you for 10 episodes."
While Turner wasn't physically present at the Comic-Con panel, he did send a video message, which glitched out and eventually lead to a teaser of the show.
"We're building something special with Neuromancer," Turner said. "[Gibson] didn’t just give us cyberspace, he helped us define the entire cyperpunk genre. This is just your first access point."
"The future is in your mind."
Check out the official teaser for Apple TV's Neuromancer. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/gOqHiavOpv
The trailer, which is now live on YouTube , shows a good look at Briana Middleton as Molly with her mirror eyes and deadly fingernails that earn her the moniker 'razorgirl,' the cyberpunk setting of the story, and, of course, Mark Strong as Armitage. It's dark, gritty, and intense.
This is the latest big reveal for Neuromancer after Apple TV+ shared a first look at the series with a 25-second clip two weeks ago. In the clip , someone (presumably Case) pushes a button on a retro computer console. The camera then pans up to a TV screen, which displays the words 'Ashpool-1' and the opening line of Gibson's novel: "The sky above the port was the color of television, tuned to a dead channel."
